# dbd — Database Designer

> A standalone CLI and embeddable Rust library for managing database schemas as code.

dbd parses SQL DDL files, resolves dependencies, generates migrations, loads data, and deploys to PostgreSQL, Supabase, SQLite, or Convex — all from a single binary with zero runtime dependencies.

## Core concept

SQL files are the source of truth. Path = `ddl/<type>/<schema>/<name>.<ext>` (roles have no schema): `<type>` ∈ table|view|materialized_view|function|procedure|enum|sequence|role, ext `.ddl`|`.sql`. Folder = type, parent = schema, filename = entity name. Singular type folder is canonical (plural accepted but `dbd doctor --fix` migrates it to singular).
- `ddl/table/config/lookups.ddl` → entity `config.lookups` (table)
- `ddl/view/config/genders.ddl` → entity `config.genders` (view)
- `ddl/materialized_view/analytics/daily_sales.ddl` → entity `analytics.daily_sales` (materialized view; write `create materialized view if not exists …` + trailing `create [unique] index …`)
- `ddl/procedure/staging/import_lookups.ddl` → entity `staging.import_lookups` (procedure)

Files are parsed once into a rich internal representation (Entity + TableDef). That same structure drives every feature: dependency graph, apply, migrations, DBML generation, data import.

## design.yaml structure

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject

source:
  dialect: postgresql

target:                        # ONLY the first entry is read; the URL scheme picks the adapter
  postgres:                    # key `supabase` = same adapter + Supabase rules (see below)
    url: $DATABASE_URL         # -d / $DATABASE_URL override it
    extensions: [uuid-ossp]
    roles:
      - name: app_user
    skip_schemas: [auth]       # target owns these schemas — exclude their entities from the design
    grants:                    # {schema: {role: [perms]}} — any target key, applied by apply + deploy
      config: { app_user: [usage, select] }

schemas:
  - config
  - staging:
      grants: { app_user: [usage, select] }   # merges with target.grants
      exposed: false           # served by PostgREST? drives inspect's RLS report

apply:                         # lifecycle hooks around the DDL phase
  after:                       # runs on `apply` AND `deploy`, before the grants and policies/
    - script: sql/realtime.sql
      writes: [app.messages]   # declare tables dbd cannot derive by parsing

import:                        # data files are found by convention: import/[<env>/]<schema>/<table>.<csv|tsv|json|jsonl>
  options: { truncate: true, null_value: '' }
  tables:                      # per-table overrides only — NOT an allowlist
    - staging.legacy: { null_value: '\N' }
  after: [import/loader.sql]   # runs on `dbd import` and `dbd deploy` — NOT on `dbd apply`

export:                        # empty ⇒ every table; listed ⇒ only these (tables, views or matviews)
  - config.lookups

materialized_views:            # refresh scheduling for ddl/materialized_view/ entities (pg_cron)
  options:                     # shared defaults for every matview
    refresh: "0 2 * * *"       # cron expression; omit ⇒ no scheduled refresh
    concurrently: true         # needs a unique index on the matview
  overrides:                   # per-matview overrides (by qualified name)
    analytics.top_products: { refresh: "*/30 * * * *" }

dbml:
  base:
    exclude: { schemas: [staging] }
  core:
    include: { schemas: [config] }
    output: core.dbml          # filename (default: <key>.dbml)
    auto_group_by_schema: true # emit `TableGroup <schema>` per schema
    groups:                    # or explicit groups (precedence over auto)
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]

scopes:                        # named entity subsets — deploy one design to many DBs
  hub:
    includes: [config, app.users]   # schema | schema.entity | schema.* (wildcard)
    deps: report               # report (default, errors on gaps) | include (auto-closure)
    extensions: []             # optional per-scope allowlist; omit=all, []=none, [vector]=subset
  reporting:
    excludes: [staging.*]      # wildcard drops a schema's entities but keeps the schema
  everything: all              # bare `all` = the full set; `all`/`default` are reserved names

ignore: [bfs, my_company.*]    # exact names or prefix.* — matching references are not resolved

format: { keyword_case: lower, query_style: river }   # dbd format options
```

Parsed but not read (reserved): `import.staging`, `import.options.format`, `import.tables[].env`, `target.schemas`, `target.path`, `external[].columns`.

**The `supabase` target key** uses the same PostgreSQL adapter but (1) exposes `public` by default, (2) keeps Supabase's schemas (`auth`, `storage`, `realtime`, `graphql_public`, `supabase_functions`, `pgbouncer`, `pgsodium`, `vault`, `extensions`, `supabase_migrations`) out of `reconcile --prune`, (3) adds `GRANT USAGE` to `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` on every listed schema when any grants are configured, and (4) is the default protected set for `dbd reset` (which also protects `public`). `source.dialect: supabase` is just PostgreSQL for the reader.

Scopes are orthogonal to `target` (DB platform) and the connection: pair them at run time with `dbd deploy --scope hub --database $HUB_URL`. `includes`/`excludes` items are a bare schema (its entities + the schema entity), a qualified `schema.entity`, or a `schema.*` wildcard (same `prefix.*` syntax as `ignore:`; drops a schema's entities while keeping the schema — for `includes`, `schema.*` ≡ `schema`). A dependency gap (in-scope entity referencing a managed entity outside the scope) is an error under `report`; `external:` entities are never gaps. An optional per-scope `extensions:` allowlist restricts which `target.extensions` apply (omit ⇒ all, `[]` ⇒ none, `[vector]` ⇒ subset) — for deploying to a DB that lacks an extension; roles/externals stay always-on. Omit `default`/the block ⇒ full set; `--scope all` is always the full set. Sequences are selected like tables; a table depends on the enum its column is typed with, the sequence its default draws from and the function a trigger in its file runs (gaps reported, pulled in under `include`); a scope keeps the schema an allowed extension installs into; grants follow the scope (a scoped apply/deploy grants only on the schemas it builds); roles and pg_cron refresh jobs are not narrowed. Every scope-announcing command prints `scope 'X': N of M entities` (working set incl. the `include` closure, out of every entity, externals left out). **A scope narrows what is applied, not what the project owns:** `reconcile --prune --scope` never drops a table the design declares outside the scope — upgrade to ≥0.24.1 before a scoped prune (earlier releases did, #40). **Scope guard:** the first `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile` pins a database to its resolved scope (recorded in the bookkeeping table's `scope` column — `dbd.meta.scope` on Postgres/Supabase, `_dbd_meta.scope` on SQLite); a later `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile`/`reset` under a *different* scope is refused unless you pass `--allow-scope-change` (which re-pins the DB) — `reset --force` also bypasses it. Pre-existing DBs are unpinned until their next write.

## Commands

- `dbd init` — scaffold project (`--target postgres|supabase`; any other target is refused); or **reverse-engineer** a whole project + baseline snapshot from an existing source: `--from-db <conn>` (live DB; a database with both `auth` and `storage` schemas gets a `supabase` target) or `--from-dbml <file>` (DBML, mutually exclusive; `--target postgres|supabase`). Refuses against a dbd-managed DB (use `merge`) or an existing `design.yaml`. Flags: `--schema`/`--exclude-schema`/`--all-schemas`/`--roles`/`--version`/`--dry-run`; secrets stay out (`$DATABASE_URL`)
- `dbd merge` — sync a DB (or `--from-dbml <file>`) into the current project (reverse-engineer + reconcile, never edits `design.yaml`): foreign or managed `D≥Y` → overwrite DDL + auto-snapshot the diff; managed `D<Y` → refuse (stale DB, no override); orphans reported never deleted; same selection flags as init
- `dbd inspect` — validate, report errors/warnings (+ scope dependency gaps with `--scope`, its advisory checks run over the scope, and a `deps: include` closure that needs what the scope excludes is refused); `--fix` auto-formats DDL files in place (`--fix --scope` only the scope's files); `-n` naming nothing is `no entity named 'X'`, and under a scope one it does not build `X is outside scope 'S'` (same on apply/graph/export/refresh); `--from-db` resolves references against the live catalog (uses `-d`/`--database`) and caches to `.dbd/refcache.json`. Surfaces unresolved migration `-- TODO:`s. **Exits 1 on blocking errors** (v0.12.0+; previously always 0), so it works as a CI gate — a parse error also states that `apply`/`reconcile`/`deploy` will refuse until fixed. Under `--scope`, errors are split into blocking vs `Out of scope — not blocking '<scope>'` by the same rule the run uses, so `inspect` and `apply` agree; out-of-scope errors don't affect the exit code but are never suppressed. Also prints an advisory `Suggestions:` section (Postgres/Supabase) for string-set `CHECK` constraints that could be enums — advisory only, never affects validity/exit code; proposals are grouped by value set, table-qualified on a name clash, and an identifier that is not a safe path segment is reported without a path
- `dbd apply` — apply schemas + entities + pending migrations (blocks while migration TODOs remain) in one dependency sort (type bands: schema, extension, role, sequence, enum, table, view, matview, function/procedure; a real dependency can push an entity later), in ONE transaction on PostgreSQL (`DBD_NO_TX` opts out); then matview stamping (drift stamps in `dbd.matview_stamps`, never the matview's own COMMENT), pg_cron sync, `apply.after`, then the configured grants (under `--scope` only on the schemas it builds); `apply.before` runs outside the transaction. `--with-policies` also applies RLS. `--dry-run` prints the order (no grants, no hooks) after running apply's own gates — it refuses an unparseable file, a gap/closure conflict or an unknown `-n` exactly where apply would — and honours the scope's `extensions:` allowlist
- `dbd import` — load staging data (CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL; a `.json` file is a JSON array of records or JSON Lines — on Convex an array only; CSV/TSV header skipped and columns by position on PostgreSQL, by header name on SQLite; data files are read as UTF-8) from the `import/` convention; env-specific files under `import/<env>/<schema>/` load only when `-e <env>` matches. Truncate (`TRUNCATE` on PostgreSQL, `DELETE FROM` on SQLite; Convex's `--replace` always replaces, so `truncate: false` has no effect there) → load → call the procedures that read each staging table (only procedures are loaders — a function is never run) → `import.after`. `-n <table> -f <file>` loads one explicit file (format from `.jsonl`/`.json`/`.tsv`, else CSV) and nothing else — no truncate, procedures or `import.after`; under `--scope` a declared table must be one the scope builds, an undeclared one loads with a warning. Under `--scope` an entry needs every table its procedure writes and its declared staging table. Nothing is skipped silently (`--dry-run` included): the summary always states the table count (including `0`) and warns with the reason — no `import/` dir, files belonging to another `-e <env>`, a staging file that failed to parse, an entry cut by `--scope` (`X not imported — T is outside scope 'S'`), a `-n` name matching no staging file, or a function that reads a staging table no procedure loads (`X has no loader procedure — function F reads it but is not run`)
- `dbd export` — export table data (scope-aware) to `export/<schema>/<name>.<fmt>`; `-f/--format` sets the format (`csv`/`tsv`/`jsonl`; any other is refused), `-o/--output <dir>` the destination dir (`<dir>/<name>.<fmt>`, e.g. straight into `import/` for a round-trip — JSONL round-trips too). Empty `export:` ⇒ every table; a list ⇒ only those — tables, views or matviews (a view exports the rows its query returns: views that dereference FKs to the staging tables' natural keys move a long-lived system's data to a new database). An entry naming nothing exportable is warned about; a `-n` that selects nothing is an error
- `dbd refresh` — run `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY]` now (honoring each matview's resolved `concurrently`); `-n <entity>` or `-n <schema>.*` targets a subset, omit for all. Scheduled refresh is otherwise managed in-database via pg_cron (jobs named `dbd:refresh:<schema>.<name>`, synced on `apply`/`deploy`; needs the `pg_cron` extension)
- `dbd deploy --source owner/repo/path` — fetch + apply + grants (scoped) + import + policies (`deploy` = bring the DB fully up from source, so RLS from `policies/` applies unconditionally, unlike `apply`'s opt-in `--with-policies`; grants are the same `apply` applies, right after the schema). `deploy` is the ONLY command that takes a GitHub source (`owner/repo[/path][@ref]` or a github.com URL); others refuse one — clone and pass the path. `GITHUB_TOKEN` (private repos) is sent as a bearer token to `api.github.com` only. Honours `-c`. GitHub sources cache under `~/.cache/dbd` — `--no-cache` re-downloads this source, `--clear-cache` wipes the whole cache first. Every phase reports its count including `0`, and a zero import states why (see `dbd import`); a failed policy file is a **warning**, not a failure — it is counted in the summary and the deploy still succeeds. `--dry-run` runs the real gates (refuses an unparseable file, a gap or closure conflict) and reports after scope filtering: the scope line, `deps: include` gaps as `+ auto-included:`, entities to apply, data files to import with the reason for each left out, policy files applied/skipped. `dbd deploy` is a thin wrapper over the library's `Design::deploy`, so an embedder gets the identical pipeline
- `dbd reconcile` — pre-release (pre-v1) **declarative** apply: diff the live DB against the design and apply `CREATE`/`ALTER` in place, no snapshots/version bump; scoped to managed schemas. `--allow-destructive` drops columns/constraints on managed tables and removes enum values (Postgres has no `ALTER TYPE … DROP VALUE`, so the type is recreated: dependent managed views dropped, defaults taken off, type renamed aside and recreated, columns moved across via `::text::`, defaults restored, old type dropped — all in one transaction, so any failure is total; a dependent materialized view is declined, never auto-dropped); `--prune` drops orphaned tables (in a managed schema, gone from the design); orphaned enums are only warned. Materialized views: create-if-absent (drift stamp recorded in `dbd.matview_stamps`); a drifted definition is only **warned**, never auto-dropped (a matview recreate is `DROP … CASCADE`, losing data/dependents — drop it manually, then `apply`/reconcile recreates it). Disabled once `project.released` (it checks only that flag). Converges columns (a `nextval('s')` default included), PK/unique, FKs, CHECKs, indexes and column comments. `public` is managed only when the design puts something there — a role or an extension with no `schema:` does not count (before 0.25 it did, and `--prune` dropped undeclared tables in `public`). Records version 0 for a design with no `project.version`. `--dry-run` refuses a database pinned to another scope
- `dbd diff` — read-only: show the complete live-DB↔design difference (columns, PK/unique, FK, CHECK, indexes, column comments, enums — the same model reconcile converges; diff also shows what reconcile won't touch: orphans without `--prune`, orphan enums, matview drift) plus **materialized-view drift** (each matview reported `missing`/`drifted`/`unstamped`/`orphan` via the `dbd:hash` drift stamp in `dbd.matview_stamps`; counts toward `--exit-code`, in `--json` as `matview_drift`). Table, view and enum comments are not compared. `--json` for tooling, `--exit-code` (0 in sync / 2 drift / 1 error). Tables + enums (structural) + matview drift; always available (even after release); refuses on scope dependency gaps
- `dbd release` (alias `dbd baseline`) — cut v1: write a baseline snapshot at the current `project.version` and set `project.released: true`, locking in the snapshot/migration workflow (disables `reconcile`). Refuses if already released or the design has errors. A project that already has snapshots (`init --from-db`/`merge` write them without setting `released`) is released at the version its latest snapshot reached, with no second baseline — refused while the design has changes no snapshot records, or `project.version` disagrees with the latest snapshot. Edits `design.yaml` in place (comments and layout kept), as `dbd snapshot` does
- `dbd combine` — combine DDL into single SQL file (scope-aware); generated statements follow the project's dialect — guarded `CREATE SCHEMA` + `GO` for T-SQL, none for MySQL/SQLite, PostgreSQL-only extensions and roles as a comment; an unparseable file is left out without a word
- `dbd emit --dialect mysql|tsql|sqlite [-f out.sql] [--report r.json]` — translate a PostgreSQL project's schema into another engine's DDL: tables with keys, FKs, CHECKs, indexes, identity/serial (`AUTO_INCREMENT`/`IDENTITY(1,1)`/`INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`), generated columns, defaults (`now()`, `current_date`, `gen_random_uuid()` translated; a literal loses its `::cast`; the rest reported) and comments where the target keeps them; views/matviews as `CREATE VIEW` with the body untranslated (reported; a matview becomes a plain view, reported, its indexes left out). T-SQL also gets `CREATE SCHEMA` and `CREATE SEQUENCE` (`nextval` → `NEXT VALUE FOR`) and ends every statement with `GO` (the sqlcmd/SSMS separator — split on it before sending through a driver); MySQL/SQLite report sequences. Functions/procedures/triggers skipped (reported); an FK to an `external:`/out-of-scope table left out (reported); a key column on unbounded text bounded (reported); an unparseable file reported as missing. CHECK, generated and index expressions/predicates pass through untranslated (reported). Enum columns become `VARCHAR(255)`/`nvarchar(255)`/`TEXT` (reported); MySQL/SQLite fold the schema into the name (`schema_table`). Still unreported: identity `START`/`INCREMENT`, lost precision/time zones. Exit 0 with downgrades — assert on the report. Refuses non-PostgreSQL projects
- `dbd graph` — dependency graph as JSON (scope-aware)
- `dbd diagram` — build the schema model and open the hosted interactive viewer (model gzip-encoded in the URL fragment, client-side only; /projects remembers opened designs in localStorage); `--print-url` prints the link, `--site`/`$DBD_DIAGRAM_URL` overrides the base, `--json -f` writes the raw SchemaModel JSON (drop the file onto /diagram) (`version: 3` — `tables` (columns incl. `identity`/`generated`, indexes with `where`, `checks`) and `refs` (every FK) for the ER view, `stubs` for the tables FKs land on that the model does not carry (`kind` `external`/`out_of_scope`/`unresolved`), `entities`/`deps` for views, routines, triggers, sequences and the call graph (`uses` = a column's enum or sequence), `schemas` = every schema the model draws something in, `note`/`noteMd` comments on every kind, `history` for the per-snapshot changelog (under `--scope`, the working set incl. the closure), `enums` with their values); a `deps: include` closure that needs what the scope excludes is refused
- `dbd dbml` — generate DBML documentation (scope-aware: `--scope` filters to the scope's working set). Carries CHECKs (`checks` block), expression indexes (backticked), table UNIQUEs (as named unique indexes), index notes (`where:`, `order:`, `nulls not distinct` lines), generated columns and ALWAYS identities (custom properties `generated always as:` / `generated as identity:`), and a stub for every referenced table it does not define, typed from the design. Needs @dbml/core ≥ 5.0 for `checks`, ≥ 9.1 for custom properties
- `dbd snapshot` — diff vs latest snapshot, generate migration SQL; smart multi-snapshot splits renames/type-changes/enum-removals into safe stages (with `*.data.sql` corrections)
- `dbd migrate` — show migration status (read-only; `--status`). Pending migrations are run by `dbd apply`, not here
- `dbd policies` — apply RLS policies from `policies/<schema>/<table>.sql` (idempotent, fail-forward). Also run unconditionally by `dbd deploy` / `Design::deploy`, and opt-in on `dbd apply --with-policies`. Scope-filtered: a policy's target is read from its path, and one whose table is outside the working set is skipped and reported rather than run against a plane that lacks its schema (a file off that layout has no derivable target and always applies)
- **Lifecycle hooks** — `apply.before` / `apply.after` run on both `apply` and `deploy` (after is post-entity, before the configured grants and `policies/`); `import.after` runs with the import phase — `dbd import` and `dbd deploy` — and **never on `dbd apply`**, so post-DDL SQL parked there silently does nothing on `dbd apply` — move it to `apply.after`. Entries are a path or `{script, writes}`; declare `writes:` when tables appear as `format()`/`array[…]` data rather than SQL identifiers, since derivation returns empty there. A hook with no derivable deps and no `writes:` always runs — scope filtering is a correctness aid, not a security boundary
- `dbd doctor` — audit/migrate config + layout: old-format design.yaml, stale files, and every non-canonical DDL folder the scanner reads → singular (`ddl/functions/`→`ddl/function/`, `sequences`, and `materialized_views`/`matviews`/`matview` → `materialized_view`; collision keeps newer, backs up older as `.bkp`). Also reports misfiled view/matview DDL (a `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` under `ddl/view/` or the reverse) with a move hint — not auto-fixed. Always exits 0
- `dbd reset` — drop the project's own objects entity-level (functions/materialized views/views/tables/sequences/enums, reverse order; matviews `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW … CASCADE` before the views/tables they read); keeps schemas + extensions by default. `--schemas`/`--extensions`/`--clean` opt into DROP SCHEMA/EXTENSION (under `--scope`, only the extensions the scope installs); `--target <postgres|supabase>` (default: the design's target key, i.e. the first `target:` entry) sets the protected-schema set (`supabase` also protects `public`; every role the design declares — `ddl/role/` and `target.roles` — is dropped on a full reset, only for `postgres`). Guarded by the bookkeeping env check (`dbd.meta` on Postgres/Supabase, `_dbd_meta` on SQLite; the `dbd` schema itself is never dropped) + the scope guard; `--scope` restricts to the scope's objects (a wrong-scope reset is refused unless `--allow-scope-change`/`--force`)
- `dbd format [--check]` — DDL formatter; river-style SELECT/VIEW bodies on by default (`query_style: river`/`none`, `gutter`); river output is AST-verified and falls back to keyword-case-only if it can't reproduce a query faithfully (CTEs, etc.). `--check` exits 1 if any file would change (drop-in for pre-commit; `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` ships `dbd-format` + `dbd-format-system`)
- `dbd install` — install dbd's Claude Code assets (the `dbd` skill + `dbd-pattern-verifier` agent, embedded in the binary) so an AI assistant knows the schema-as-code conventions. Global (`~/.claude`, or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) by default; `--project` writes `./.claude` (shared with the team only if committed); `--dry-run` previews. Reports each asset created/updated/unchanged and is idempotent

Reverse-engineering coverage (`init --from-db`/`merge`): schemas, extensions, enums, tables (columns, defaults, identity, PK/FK/unique/check constraints, indexes incl. gin/gist/brin/hash, partial and expression indexes, comments, serial/identity columns), views, materialized views (definition + indexes from `pg_matviews`, written to `ddl/materialized_view/`), functions & procedures (verbatim), roles (opt-in `--roles`), standalone sequences. Not captured: triggers. A DBML source (`--from-dbml`) = schemas/enums/tables/FKs; from dbd's own DBML, CHECKs, identity (ALWAYS vs BY DEFAULT), serial, generated columns, column UNIQUE, partial/expression indexes and key order survive, a table UNIQUE comes back as a named unique index, enum comments are lost. A SQLite source (`--from-db sqlite://…`) = tables/views/user-indexes captured verbatim from `sqlite_master` (CHECK/affinity/AUTOINCREMENT/WITHOUT ROWID preserved; no schemas/enums/functions/sequences/roles; triggers skipped). The reverse dialect (postgres vs sqlite target) is taken from the connection URL scheme.

Global flags: `-e dev|prod` (`development`/`production` accepted as aliases; anything else is an error; default `prod`) selects `import/<env>/` folders and is recorded in bookkeeping. `--scope <name>` selects a `scopes:` entity subset; `--deps report|include` overrides that scope's gap policy for one run. **Gap-gated** (filter, and refuse on a gap under `report`): `inspect`/`apply`/`import`/`deploy`/`reconcile`/`diff`. **Filter-only**: `dbml`/`combine`/`emit`/`graph`/`diagram`/`export`/`reset`/`refresh`/`policies` (`inspect --scope` is where gaps surface). **Ignored with a warning** (`--scope` or `--deps`): `snapshot`/`release`/`migrate`/`doctor`/`init`/`merge`/`format`/`install`. `snapshot`/`release`/`migrate` ignore it deliberately: a snapshot records the *design*, not one database, so a scoped baseline would omit entities and make every later snapshot emit spurious `CREATE`s. Scope decides which migration steps *run*, not which exist — a removed table's drop runs under a scope occupying its schema, where the table still exists. All filter to the entity working set (`reset` drops those entities; `--schemas` additionally restricts the dropped schemas to the scope's).

## Architecture

- Parser: libpg_query (PostgreSQL's own grammar, via the `pg_query` crate) — every DDL entity type. sqlparser-rs remains for `dbd format` and enum-candidate detection, not for reading DDL.
- Adapters (all working):
    - PostgreSQL + Supabase (sqlx, `postgres://`) — COPY streaming import, namespace-aware catalog, one transaction per apply
    - SQLite (sqlx-sqlite, `sqlite://`/`sqlite::memory:`/`file:`) — batched multi-row INSERT (≤500 rows or 32k binds per batch), trigger-aware DDL splitter, ~150 builtins + `sqlite_*` prefix recognised offline
    - Convex (codegen, `convex:`/`convex://<dir>[?deploy=true]`) — flattens names, maps SQL → `v.*` validators, enums emit `export const X = v.union(v.literal(…))` above `defineSchema`, single-column FKs emit `v.id("table")`; opt-in `npx convex deploy` after apply; `import_data` shells out to `npx convex import --replace` per table (so `truncate: false` has no effect); write the URL quoted in YAML (`url: "convex:"`)
- No MySQL or SQL Server adapter: `mysql://`/`mariadb://`/`sqlserver://`/`mssql://` URLs are refused by name. Their DDL is *read* (`tsql`/`mysql` readers: identity + references, no columns) and *written* by `dbd emit`
- Readers (`source.dialect`/`source.parser`): `pg_query` (structured — needed by diff/reconcile/emit), `tsql`, `mysql`, `verbatim` (SQLite). Every DDL reader — scan, apply, deploy, combine, format, doctor, merge, migrations — decodes UTF-8 or UTF-16 with a BOM
- Classification: adapter-owned — each adapter knows its target's catalog (Postgres queries pg_proc/pg_type, SQLite uses a sorted builtins list + `sqlite_*` prefix rule, Convex defers everything to user-defined)
- Parallel parsing: rayon for CPU-bound file parse, tokio for async DB operations
- Library-first: `dbd-core` crate for embedding, `dbd-cli` for the binary
- Reference cache: `inspect --from-db` snapshots all user-defined entities to `.dbd/refcache.json`; subsequent offline runs consult it to silence "Unresolved reference" warnings without a live DB

## Key types

- `Entity` — central type for all DDL objects
- `TableDef` — parsed table structure (columns, FKs with actions, indexes, constraints, comments)
- `EntityType` — Schema, Extension, Role, Sequence, Enum, Table, View, MaterializedView, Function, Procedure, Trigger (reported by the T-SQL/MySQL readers; dbd never applies one), External, Import
- `DatabaseAdapter` trait — connect, apply (single + batch, incl. transactional begin/commit/rollback batch), import/export (`truncate_table` for the import's truncate step), classify_reference, resolve_entity, list_entities, introspect (reverse-engineer), migration + meta tracking, `stamp_matview` (matview drift stamps)
- `RefCache` — JSON snapshot of remote entity names for offline `inspect`

## Safety

- The bookkeeping table records environment (dev/prod) and version in the database: `dbd.meta` in a dedicated `dbd` schema on Postgres/Supabase (paired with `dbd.migrations` and `dbd.matview_stamps`; not PostgREST-exposed, excluded from reverse-engineering/reset), `_dbd_meta`/`_dbd_migrations` on SQLite (no schemas there, so the prefix is the namespace). Legacy `public._dbd_meta`/`public._dbd_migrations` (and scoped-apply strays) heal into `dbd.meta`/`dbd.migrations` automatically on the next write
- `dbd reset` blocked when the database is marked prod (rows older versions wrote as `production` included — and any database applied without `-e dev` is prod), and at version ≥ 1 in any env; `--force` overrides
- `project.released` (set by `dbd release`) disables the in-place `dbd reconcile` workflow — after release, schema changes must go through snapshots + `dbd apply`
- `dbd reconcile` never touches schemas the design doesn't declare (`public` only when the design puts something there); column drops need `--allow-destructive`, whole-table (orphan) drops need `--prune`; under `--scope`, tables the design declares outside the scope are left alone, never pruned
- `--force` overrides safety guards
- For Convex (codegen target) the equivalent state lives in `<output>/.dbd_state.json`

## Skill & agent (for AI assistants)

dbd ships a Claude-Code **skill** (`dbd`, the schema-as-code mental model + workflow rules) and a **`dbd-pattern-verifier` agent** (reviews a project for convention conformance — right workflow for the release state, idempotent DDL, secrets, folder layout, enum-vs-CHECK, matview drift). Discover + install them via the `sensei.library.json` manifest, served at `https://dbd.sensei-hq.com/.well-known/sensei.library.json` (and in-repo at the root); raw files at `/skills/dbd/SKILL.md` and `/agents/dbd-pattern-verifier.md`.
